title: THE PRIESTHOOD OF BELIEVERS
mv: But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light.
mvp: “But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light.” 1 Peter 2:9
outline: The Basis And Roles of Our Priesthood
assignment: List five (5) ways you can practically represent God as His priest in your home, school, workplace or community (2X5=10 marks).

b.x: In the Old Testament, Levites were the only tribe, chosen and dedicated as priests, serving as mediators between God and His people. However, this order of priesthood changed when the veil was torn due to the sacrifice of Christ (Matthew 27:50-51). With direct access to the presence of God, every genuine believer in Christ is now a ‘priest’ unto God (Revelation 1:5-6, 5:10). Sadly, some Christians still live as though they need some middlemen between them and God. This lesson will help us understand and embrace our role as priests in Christ Jesus.

sections.h: THE BASIS AND ROLES OF OUR PRIESTHOOD

b.x: Believers’ priesthood in Christ is based on the following:
A. Christ’s sacrifice: the blood of Jesus grants us bold access to the holiest place (Hebrews 10:19-22).
B. Priestly redemption: Christ washed us from sin and made us kings and priests (Revelation 1:5-6).
C. Non-natural descent: our priesthood is not tied to Levi but to Christ, our High Priest (Hebrews 7:11-12).

As believer-priests, we, therefore, have the roles of offering spiritual sacrifices such as worship, prayers, good works, giving, and service (1 Peter 2:5), mediating through intercession by standing in the gap for families, nations, and the Church (1 Timothy 2:1), teaching and witnessing because priests are keepers of knowledge raised to share and declare God’s word (Malachi 2:7; Matthew 28:19-20), living holy lives by setting apart our lives, and representing God to the world (Leviticus 21:6; 1 Peter 1:15-16).

We have direct access (Hebrews 4:16), and this means greater responsibility. We have been called to a life of service, not status: priesthood is not about title but service in humility (John 13:14-15). We are to witness to the nations; our priesthood is to “shew forth His praises ” to a watching world (1 Peter 2:9). We are also to await our eternal role, because we shall reign with Christ as priests and kings (Revelation 5:10).
The doctrine of the priesthood of all believers is not symbolic but practical. If you are in Christ, you are already a priest; live like one daily!
